text:
Maya Chen: Hey all — getting reports that critical alert for model-serving-latency didn't page anyone. PagerBridge UI shows a bunch of events in a 'suppressed' state.

Dan Ortiz: ugh. are these suppression rules recent? which service is showing suppressed? PagerDuty or our bridge? :thinking_face:

Maya Chen: PagerBridge. The AMQP logs show webhook delivered but bridge marked it suppressed. Trying to pull logs now.

sre-bot: [automated] New suppression event: policy_id=sb-203 suppressor=auto-silence duration=24h reason=deploy-test-mode applied_by=ci-deploy-bot

Leo Park: I just tried a manual test page from the staging monitor:
```
curl -X POST https://pagerbridge.internal/api/v1/events -d '{"alert":"test"}' -H 'Content-Type: application/json'
```
Response 200, body: {"status":"suppressed","policy":"sb-203","expires_at":"2026-06-05T12:40:00Z"}

So the bridge is intentionally suppressing.

Sarah Patel: Wait — sb-203 isn't one of our long-suppress policies. That sounds like the temporary 'deploy-test-mode' we used for the canary last night. Did someone flip the global flag? @Dan Ortiz were you in the canary rollout?

Dan Ortiz: I merged the canary changes but I explicitly set TESTING_SUPPRESS_WINDOW=60 (1m). I didn't set 24h. I didn't touch sb-203. @Maya can you paste the deploy metadata?

Maya Chen: Checking deploy logs: deploy 2026-06-05T02:30:12Z -> bridge-service:release-2026.06.05-a1b2. env snapshot:
```
SUPPRESS_MODE=enabled
TESTING_SUPPRESS_WINDOW=1440  # minutes
SUPPRESS_POLICY=sb-203
DEPLOY_BY=ci-deploy-bot
```

That 1440 looks wrong. someone probably reverted units from minutes to hours during the config refactor.

ops-oncall: I'm currently listed as on-call but didn't get paged. Manual escalation attempt: called primary on-call and left voicemail. Will page escalation list via phone tree if bridge doesn't recover.

PagerBridgeBot: Webhook delivered to pagerflow v2: req_id=abc123 status=200 delivered_to=bridge service_response={"status":"suppressed","policy":"sb-203"}

Leo Park: For immediate mitigation, I can set SUPPRESS_MODE=disabled on the bridge. Should I do that? We need to avoid blasting pages if the alert is flapping though.

Sarah Patel: Confirmed that the canary config used minutes but our refactor converted to an integer interpreted as hours. So 60 -> 60 hours if we didn't also change parsing. Looks like defaulting to minutes->hours mismatch. Noted in the config PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/infra/merge/412

This is a human/config translation bug, not PagerDuty failure.

Dan Ortiz: OK. mitigation plan:
1) disable SUPPRESS_MODE on bridge (temp)
2) patch config parsing in repo and roll forward
3) run smoke pages
4) postmortem draft

I'll take 1 & 2. Doing step 1 now — restarting bridge with env SUPPRESS_MODE=disabled (rolling restart)

Maya Chen: rolling restart started. watching logs. if pages start firing, be ready for a surge.

sre-bot: [automated] bridge-service restart initiated by Dan Ortiz at 2026-06-05T02:48:10Z. Rolling restart: 3/3 done.

Leo Park: Sending a manual test alert now via the monitor (non-suppressed path).

PagerBridgeBot: Test event forwarded to PagerDuty: pd_incident=PD12345 triggered_by=manual_test severity=critical

ops-oncall: Got the page. answered. confirming reachability. :thumbsup:

Maya Chen: Nice. So production paging restored. Dan — what's the fix for the parsing?

Dan Ortiz: pushing hotfix to parse units explicitly and add an integration test for deploy env snapshots. Small PR up now, will roll forward to bridge and canary: https://git.internal/r/redwood/infra/pull/418

Patch: change env parser to accept suffixes (m/h) and default to minutes if unspecified. Also added CI check to reject ambiguous integer values.

Sarah Patel: Great. Action items for postmortem:
- root cause: config refactor changed expected units -> ambiguous integer interpreted as hours
- impact: 24h suppression of critical alerts for model-serving-latency; on-call not paged; manual escalation required
- remediation: rolled restart to disable suppressor; hotfix to parser; add CI validation; add alert that suppression > 120 minutes requires manual confirmation
- owner: Dan Ortiz for fix, Maya Chen for detection + playbook update

I'll start the postmortem doc and tag infra and oncall leads.

Maya Chen: small follow-ups: add a dashboard tile for 'suppression policies applied' and a short runbook step to check bridge suppression state during handoffs.

Dan Ortiz: ack. I'll also add a temporary alert into the monitor that fires if any suppression policy applies to critical alerts for > 5m.

Leo Park: Leaving a note for customer-impact assessment: we had ~3 customers open support chats complaining about delayed responses in the timeframe. CS already notified and started mitigation messages. Sarah, can you sync with CS on language?

Sarah Patel: Yup. I'll coordinate messaging; suggest we say: transient alerting gap due to deployment config issue, paging restored, no data loss, investigating cause and mitigation.

Maya Chen: Thanks team. Marking this thread as resolved once PR is merged and a postmortem is posted. Adding :white_check_mark: reaction.

sre-bot: [automated] Thread auto-summary created: suppression-misconfig-2026-06-05. Postmortem checklist created in /incidents/postmortems/ (stub).
